subject: Post-demo: procurement & commercial path (PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated vs private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmefin.com>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@acmefin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement & commercial path (PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Hi Elena / Sanjay 

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on procurement readiness and the commercial path: 

What we discussed
- Scope: Redwood hosted API for initial pilot (chat + embeddings) with the option to move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for production.
- Key buyer questions: PO vs card; marketplace options; commit vs on-demand pricing; timeline for procurement/contracting.

Questions / asks for you
1) Do you prefer Purchase Order (PO) for enterprise purchases or will a company card work for pilot spend?
2) Are you interested in pursuing a marketplace route (AWS Marketplace) to facilitate PO procurement?
3) Any procurement timeline constraints (procurement/legal review windows)?

What I can do next
- Share an initial commercial quote and a short SOW (attached).
- Set up a procurement & legal sync with our contracts team if you want to review T&Cs and SOC2 evidence.
- Schedule a short technical workshop to scope Dedicated vs Private requirements if you plan to evaluate those.

Attached: Redwood_Quote_ACME-2026Q1.pdf (quote), SOW-Acme.docx (draft SOW)

Suggested next step: quick procurement sync w/ your finance + our contracts. Does Thursday 3/25 10am PT work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132


Redwood_Quote_ACME-2026Q1.pdf (attached)  line-item summary and three commercial paths: hosted on-demand, dedicated reserved commit, private deployment license.

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@acmefin.com>

Date: 2026-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement & commercial path (PO vs card, hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Marissa 

Thanks for the demo and the clear summary. A few answers from procurement/finance perspective: 

- PO preferred for any production/contractual spend. For pilot budgets we sometimes use a company card, but given the expected monthly run rate we will likely go PO.
- Marketplace is attractive; it makes procurement easier for our finance org if we can consume via AWS Marketplace and raise a PO against that.
- Timeline: our procurement team typically needs 36 weeks for contract review (depends on redlines). We will need SOC2 + security questionnaire responses as part of the evaluation.
- For capacity: cost predictability is important  our budget owner (Sanjay Mehta, cc'd) favors a committed capacity path if it reduces unit cost. That said, we want to validate accuracy/latency before a long commit.

I'll send over our vendor security questionnaire separately. Can we do the procurement sync on Friday 3/26 10am ET?

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement, Acme Financial
elena.torres@acmefin.com

- I will book the procurement sync for Fri 3/26 10am ET (inviting our contracts + finance).
- We will provide SOC2 evidence and the security questionnaire answers in advance of the call.
- We will prepare two commercial paths for discussion: (A) short pilot on hosted (card or PO for pilot), (B) committed Dedicated 12-month reserved capacity for production (PO via direct contracting or marketplace).

- Confirm a committed pricing band for Dedicated (12-mo commit) vs on-demand hosted pricing.
- Confirm whether we can support an AWS Marketplace listing to enable PO flow and whether that changes pricing or billing terms.
- Estimated lead time for provisioning Dedicated and Private deployments.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME procurement  pricing/packaging options (need confirm before Friday)

Aditya / Dev 

Looping you in to prepare for the procurement sync with Acme (Fri 3/26 10am ET). Summary of asks from Elena: PO preference, marketplace interest, SOC2 + questionnaire required, procurement timeline 36 weeks, buyer favors committed capacity for predictability but wants pilot validation.

We need a concise set of commercial options to present on Friday: 
Option 1  Hosted (SaaS)
- Billing: monthly on-demand; card or invoice (NET 30).
- Pricing: baseline per-token and per-embedding rates; minimal commitment.
- Pros: fastest to start, no provisioning lead time.
- Cons: higher unit cost, less isolation.

Option 2  Dedicated (Reserved Capacity)
- Billing: 12-month commit (quarterly invoices) or annual prepay.
- Pricing: ~3040% discount off on-demand depending on commit level (tbd).
- Pros: predictable unit economics, data isolation, SLA-backed latency/uptime.
- Provisioning lead time: estimate 24 weeks after contract + payment.

Option 3  Private (VPC / On-prem)
- Billing: enterprise license + support/ops fee (annual).
- Pricing: custom, typically higher TCO but meets strict compliance.
- Provisioning lead time: 812 weeks (hardware & networking dependent).

Marketplace / PO notes: can we enable AWS Marketplace listing (SaaS or AMI) to let Acme raise a PO? If so, confirm any pricing or billing term constraints.

Can you reply with concrete numbers (or ranges) for the commit discount and confirm lead-times so I can finalize the slide and SOW for Friday?

Thanks  I want to keep the procurement sync focused on procurement process + which commercial path they prefer.

Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME procurement  pricing/packaging options (need confirm before Friday)

Marissa 

Thanks for the summary. Confirming proposed packaging and adding concrete guidance for Friday: 

1) Hosted (SaaS)  On-demand
- Billing: monthly invoices (NET 30) or card for pilot.
- Pricing: list rates (chat generation): $0.012 / 1k tokens; embeddings: $0.0012 / 1k vectors.
- Pilot offer: 90-day pilot cap $10k (card or PO) to validate latency/quality.

2) Dedicated  12-month commit (recommended for Acme)
- Commit tiers: $50k/mo commit -> ~35% discount off on-demand; $100k/mo commit -> ~42% discount.
- Billing: quarterly invoicing via PO accepted (we can also support AWS Marketplace private offers if needed).
- Provisioning: 24 weeks after signed order + initial payment.

3) Private (VPC / On-prem)
- Model: enterprise license + annual support; baseline starts at $350k/year + integration fees.
- Provisioning: 812 weeks (hardware ordering + network).

Marketplace & PO: we can support AWS Marketplace listing (SaaS and private offers). Marketplace can accept PO-based purchasing via Private Offers which makes finance teams happy  it does add a ~23 week setup for legal & marketplace listing, but it avoids custom invoicing. Pricing via marketplace would generally match our committed pricing (we can do a private offer).

Recommendation: propose a 90-day hosted pilot (PO or card) to validate accuracy/latency, paired with a conditional 12-month Dedicated commitment (with agreed commit level) that will convert after pilot with credit for pilot spend toward the commit if they choose to convert. This addresses Acme's desire for predictability while lowering their risk.

Attachments: pricing-packaging-sheet.xlsx (updated), Redwood_marketplace-notes.pdf

I can join the procurement call Friday.

Aditya
Principal Commercial GTM | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
